criteria.text: The response concludes that Gliluv's 30-day window to object to Seller's Closing Statement expired on or about March 11, 2026, before the board resolved on March 20, 2026 to dispute the overstatement, so the Closing Statement is final and binding and the $1.9M working-capital claim is lost or at serious risk.

The response identifies the expired objection window issue as arising under Stock Purchase Agreement Section 2.4(b), or under that section read with the Board Written Consent's recital of the February 9, 2026 delivery date.
For the expired objection window issue, the response explains why it matters to Gliluv and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Transition Services Agreement makes Gliluv (as Recipient) liable to indemnify Dreisend (as Provider) without any cap, including for Losses caused by Dreisend's own ordinary negligence.
The response identifies the uncapped indemnity as appearing in Transition Services Agreement Section 8.3.
For the uncapped TSA indemnity issue, the response explains why it matters to Gliluv and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Escrow Agreement limits Gliluv's recovery for the Section 9.2(c) Environmental Indemnity to the $6.4M escrow fund, even though the SPA excludes that indemnity from the Seller cap.
hints: sole and exclusive source of recovery

criteria.text: The response identifies the environmental cap conflict as appearing in Escrow Agreement Section 5.3.
For the escrow-cap conflict with the environmental carve-out, the response explains why it matters to Gliluv and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the tax representations and the Pre-Closing Tax indemnity survive only six months after the Closing Date (i.e., until about July 15, 2026), too short for tax liabilities likely to surface on audit.
hints: six (6) months after the Closing Date

criteria.text: The response identifies the tax survival gap as appearing in Stock Purchase Agreement Section 9.1, alone or together with Section 9.2(d) or 9.4.
For the tax survival gap issue, the response explains why it matters to Gliluv and recommends a fix.
hints: 60 days after the statute of limitations

criteria.text: The response concludes that Dreisend is free to assign or delegate the TSA and/or the SPA without Gliluv's consent, because the assignment restriction binds only Buyer.
The response identifies the unrestricted Seller assignment issue as appearing in Transition Services Agreement Section 12.4, or in SPA Section 11.5 as incorporated by that section.
For the unrestricted Seller assignment issue, the response explains why it matters to Gliluv and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Escrow Amount is $6,400,000.
The response states that the Closing Date was January 15, 2026.
The response is a memo that presents its findings as discrete issues, each with a document and section reference, an explanation of significance to Gliluv, and a recommended fix.
The response claims that Gliluv's objection to the Closing Statement can still be timely delivered under SPA Section 2.4(b) as of the board's March 20, 2026 consent.
The response claims that Gliluv retains uncapped direct recourse against Dreisend for the Environmental Indemnity, without noting that Escrow Agreement Section 5.3 limits recovery to the escrow fund.
